item.title: Social issues
item.description: Talking about problems in society and how people help.

children.definition: the state of being very poor
children.example: Education is one of the best ways out of poverty.

children.definition: the situation when people want a job but cannot find one
children.example: Youth unemployment is a serious problem in many countries.

children.definition: an unfair situation in which some people have more money, rights or chances than others
children.example: The report looks at inequality between cities and villages.
The charity gives hot meals to homeless people.

children.definition: an organisation that collects money to help people in need
children.example: She gives part of her salary to a children's charity.

children.definition: to offer to do work without being paid
children.example: Students volunteer at the local hospital every Saturday.

children.definition: to make a serious effort to deal with a difficult problem
children.example: The city is building new bus lanes to tackle traffic.

children.definition: treating a person or group unfairly because of who they are
children.example: The law protects workers from discrimination.

children.definition: easily hurt or harmed, physically or emotionally
children.example: Elderly people who live alone are especially vulnerable in winter.

children.definition: to help people know and understand more about a problem
children.example: The campaign aims to raise awareness of road safety.

children.definition: the people who live in one area, or a group of people with something in common
children.example: In our mahalla, the community helps families who are in need.

children.definition: to give money or goods to help people
children.example: We donated our old clothes to a local charity.
